narrativeReportMd:
# Goal R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps `Goal` as the same resource, but local Goal content has several hard R4-to-R6 instance breaks: `statusReason`, `statusDate`, `expressedBy`, `outcomeCode`, and `outcomeReference` are no longer present under those names. R6 also adds optional structures and wider reference/terminology domains that create meaningful R6-to-R4 down-conversion risk.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions and directly relevant local Goal ValueSets/CodeSystems. Inherited base-resource and base-datatype snapshot changes were excluded.

## Main migration themes
The main themes are status model restructuring, authorship/source restructuring, removal of explicit outcome fields, and new R6-only stakeholder acceptance/sustainment semantics. Strict validators and generated R4 model classes will reject removed R4 property names in R6, while strict R4 validators will reject R6-only structures, new reference targets, and the new `Goal.lifecycleStatus` code `unknown`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact local findings are the removal of outcome fields with no obvious core replacement, the replacement of free-text `statusReason` with repeating coded `lifecycleStatusReason`, the narrowing/renaming of `statusDate` to `achievementStatusDate`, and the replacement of `expressedBy` with `source` plus a new `recorder` element.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important where source data must be interpreted: deciding whether an R4 `statusDate` is really an achievement date, whether R4 outcome data should become Observations, extensions, notes, or external links, and how to preserve free-text status reasons.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most disruptive changes could have been made less breaking by retaining deprecated aliases or adding optional new fields while preserving old ones through one major release. The R6 model is more expressive, but cross-version transforms are not fully mechanical without a ConceptMap or narrative guidance.

## Follow-up analysis
Follow-up should cover base `Resource`/`DomainResource` inherited changes, external terminology expansions, and any official cross-version ConceptMaps or narrative migration notes for Goal.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `Goal` has hard local R4-to-R6 breaks because several R4 element names were removed or replaced. Top migration concerns are preserving outcomes, interpreting status dates/reasons, and separating old `expressedBy` into R6 `source` and possibly `recorder`. The biggest uncertainty is the absence of official cross-version mapping guidance.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should not rely on simple same-name copying. R4 instances containing `statusReason`, `statusDate`, `expressedBy`, `outcomeCode`, or `outcomeReference` need transforms before R6 validation. R6 instances using `acceptance`, `continuous`, `lifecycleStatus=unknown`, new `addresses` target resources, or source/recorder patterns cannot be losslessly represented in plain R4 without extensions or external resources.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, type, reference target, binding, and flag deltas because they are directly visible in the local StructureDefinitions. Confidence is medium for the intended semantic mapping of removed/replaced elements because no official diff, narrative rationale, or cross-version ConceptMap was supplied.

findings.title: Goal.statusReason was replaced by repeating CodeableConcept lifecycleStatusReason

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `Goal.statusReason` as a single string.

semanticText.definition: Captures the reason for the current status.
semanticText.comment: This will typically be captured for statuses such as rejected, on-hold or cancelled, but could be present for others.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the status reason was a scalar free-text string at `Goal.statusReason`.

newState.summary: R6 has optional repeating `Goal.lifecycleStatusReason` as CodeableConcept with an example binding.

binding.description: Example binding to R6 Goal status reason value set.

semanticText.definition: Captures the reason for the current lifecycle status.
semanticText.comment: This will typically be captured for statuses such as rejected, on-hold or cancelled, but could be present for others.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the analogous concept is a repeating `CodeableConcept` named `lifecycleStatusReason`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element name changed from a generic status reason to an explicit lifecycle status reason, and the R4/R6 definitions and comments are nearly identical apart from the lifecycle qualifier.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `statusReason` will fail strict R6 validation because that element no longer exists. Generated R4 code that reads or writes `statusReason` must be updated to use a repeating `CodeableConcept`. R6-to-R4 conversion can preserve a single text-only reason by using `CodeableConcept.text`, but coded and repeated reasons are not cleanly representable in the old scalar string field.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Status reasons can explain rejected, cancelled, or on-hold goals; dropping them can change care-planning interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Make lifecycle status reasons coded and repeatable instead of free text.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `statusReason` while adding repeating coded `lifecycleStatusReason`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: a repeating `CodeableConcept` can represent coded and multiple lifecycle-status reasons better than a single string. A less-breaking base design exists, but it would leave the old free-text field next to the new coded field for the same fact. Because that duplication creates real validation and interoperability ambiguity, the breaking replacement is probably justified, though a staged deprecation would have been more compatible.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would keep R4 `statusReason` as an optional deprecated string and add R6 `lifecycleStatusReason` for coded or repeated reasons. Existing R4 instances would remain valid and could gradually map text into `CodeableConcept.text`. The tradeoff is a same-resource dual representation: when both are populated, systems need precedence and consistency rules, and the deprecated representation may never fully disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but creates duplicate same-resource representations, precedence rules, and a deprecated free-text field that may persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Goal.statusReason` as 0..1 string with definition `Captures the reason for the current status.`
R6 defines `Goal.lifecycleStatusReason` as 0..* CodeableConcept with an example binding to `goal-status-reason`.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments show only the fields relevant to this finding plus required Goal context.

findings.narrativeMd: `Goal.statusReason` is not present in R6. The replacement is not just a rename: it changes a single free-text string into a repeating `CodeableConcept`. Existing R4 data that uses the old property needs a transform before R6 validation, and applications need to handle arrays and codings rather than a scalar string.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances with `statusReason` become R6-invalid under strict validation because unknown elements are not allowed. R6 instances with multiple or coded `lifecycleStatusReason` values cannot be losslessly represented as R4 `statusReason`; a converter can place a single textual reason into the old string, but coding/system/display details and multiple reasons require extensions or data loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `statusReason` to `lifecycleStatusReason[0].text` unless local rules can code it. For R6-to-R4, decide whether to concatenate text, select one reason, or preserve full structured reasons in extensions. Test cancelled, rejected, on-hold, coded, text-only, and repeated cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The model improvement was likely to support codable and multiple reasons, but a deprecated old string could have avoided a hard element-removal break. The tradeoff would be temporary duplication and ambiguity when both the old and new representations are present.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 value set is example strength, so codes outside the listed SNOMED examples are still allowed; the main break is element identity and representation, not required terminology validation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Goal.statusReason` is removed and the closest R6 element is `Goal.lifecycleStatusReason`, changing the wire name, type from `string` to `CodeableConcept`, and cardinality from `0..1` to `0..*`. That is a real old-valid/new-invalid break and generated code using the scalar string must change. The forward migration path is still fairly direct for ordinary R4 data: put the old string into one `CodeableConcept.text`. The R6 design also adds useful coded and repeated reasons, so the compatibility cost looks proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Goal.statusReason: 0..1 string, definition 'Captures the reason for the current status.'
R6 StructureDefinition Goal.lifecycleStatusReason: 0..* CodeableConcept, same status-reason role with example binding to goal-status-reason
No local cross-version mapping file was found outside the R4/R6 StructureDefinition evidence
freshReview.fmmEffect: Goal is FMM 2 and trial-use, so stability expectations are meaningful but neutral; the concrete mechanism matters more than the maturity label.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 instances with statusReason fail strict R6 validation, and SDKs change from one string property to a repeating CodeableConcept property.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking base design would keep deprecated statusReason while adding lifecycleStatusReason. It would preserve old instances, but it creates duplicate same-resource representations and precedence/consistency rules, so it is not clearly lower cost than a straightforward transform.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the break is real, but I would treat it as proportionate rather than a design that must be revisited.

findings.title: Goal.statusDate was replaced by achievementStatusDate with narrower semantics

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `Goal.statusDate` as the date the current status took effect.

semanticText.definition: Identifies when the current status. I.e. When initially created, when achieved, when cancelled, etc.
semanticText.comment: To see the date for past statuses, query history.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `statusDate` could describe the effective date of lifecycle-like states such as creation, achievement, cancellation, or other current status changes.

newState.summary: R6 has optional `Goal.achievementStatusDate` for when the current achievement status took effect.

semanticText.short: When goal achievement status took effect
semanticText.definition: Identifies when the current achievement status took effect. I.e. When achieved, when improving, etc.
semanticText.comment: To see the date for past statuses, query history.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `achievementStatusDate` is specifically tied to `achievementStatus`, not to all lifecycle status transitions.

facts.oldValue: current status date including initially created, achieved, cancelled, etc.
facts.newValue: current achievement status date including achieved, improving, etc.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The W5 mapping remains `FiveWs.recorded` and the type/cardinality are the same, but the R6 definition narrows the concept from generic status to achievement status.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance with `statusDate` is invalid as R6 because the old element name is gone. Even after renaming, the meaning can be wrong if the R4 date recorded a lifecycle event such as cancellation or initial creation rather than achievement progress.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly reclassifying cancellation or creation dates as achievement dates could mislead care-planning timelines.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate achievement status timing from lifecycle status timing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `statusDate` with clarified lifecycle-status semantics and add `achievementStatusDate` for achievement timing.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating achievement-status timing from lifecycle-status timing is a reasonable R6 goal, but removing the broader R4 `statusDate` leaves lifecycle transition dates such as cancellation or initial creation without an equivalent base Goal element. The same goal could have been met by retaining the old field with clearer semantics and adding the achievement-specific field, so the hard rename/removal was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible R6 design could keep `Goal.statusDate` as the lifecycle-status effective date and introduce `Goal.achievementStatusDate` for achievement progress. This preserves existing R4 instances and makes the new distinction explicit. The main tradeoff is that implementers must understand two related date fields and follow consistency guidance when both lifecycle and achievement dates are recorded.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains a broad legacy name and needs guidance when both dates are present, but preserves R4 data with modest long-term cost.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `statusDate` as 0..1 date for when the current status took effect.
R6 defines `achievementStatusDate` as 0..1 date for when the current achievement status took effect.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is only safe if the old date truly describes the achievement status. It is not safe for lifecycle cancellation or creation dates without review.

findings.narrativeMd: `Goal.statusDate` disappeared and the closest R6 element is `Goal.achievementStatusDate`. This is a hard property-name break and also a semantic narrowing: R4 explicitly mentioned creation, achievement, and cancellation, while R6 only covers achievement-status timing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances carrying `statusDate` are invalid in R6 until transformed. R6 `achievementStatusDate` can be placed into R4 `statusDate`, but that back-conversion loses the R6 distinction that the date is specifically about achievement status.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not blindly rename every `statusDate`. If the Goal lifecycle status is `completed` and the date reflects achievement, map to `achievementStatusDate`. If the date reflects cancellation, rejection, initial creation, or another lifecycle transition, preserve it in an extension, Provenance, history, or another local migration field and flag for review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The clearer achievement-specific field is useful, but removing the broader old field was avoidable. Keeping a deprecated lifecycle-status date alongside the new achievement date would have preserved R4 data while enabling more precise R6 semantics.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Official narrative or cross-version maps would materially improve confidence about whether an R6 lifecycle-status date was intentionally omitted or represented elsewhere.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Goal.statusDate` is a lifecycle-status effective date, including creation, achievement, cancellation, and similar status changes. R6 removes that path and adds `achievementStatusDate`, which is only for achievement-status timing. An R4 cancellation or creation date cannot safely be renamed without changing meaning, and old instances using `statusDate` are not valid R6 as-is. This looks like more than a naming cleanup because it drops the lifecycle-status date use case.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Goal.statusDate: 0..1 date, 'When initially created, when achieved, when cancelled, etc.'
R6 StructureDefinition Goal.achievementStatusDate: 0..1 date, 'When achieved, when improving, etc.'
Both elements have W5 mapping FiveWs.recorded, but the R6 definition narrows the semantic scope
freshReview.fmmEffect: Goal is FMM 2/trial-use, which does not impose a high normative bar, but it also does not excuse a lossy semantic replacement when a modest-compatible design exists.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus semantic/documentation: R4 statusDate is an unknown R6 property, and mapping it to achievementStatusDate can misstate lifecycle events as achievement-status dates.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design could keep statusDate for lifecycle-status timing and add achievementStatusDate for achievement timing. The tradeoff is two related date fields and consistency guidance, but the old and new meanings are distinct enough that this seems manageable.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Yes alternative judgment; the independent evidence supports a hard property break plus semantic narrowing with a plausible lower-cost base design.

findings.title: Goal.expressedBy was replaced by source and a new recorder element

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `Goal.expressedBy` for the person responsible for establishing the goal.

semanticText.definition: Indicates whose goal this is - patient goal, practitioner goal, etc.
semanticText.comment: This is the individual responsible for establishing the goal, not necessarily who recorded it. (For that, use the Provenance resource.).

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `expressedBy` for the source or establishing party and directed recorder information to Provenance.

newState.summary: R6 uses `Goal.source` for the establishing party and adds `Goal.recorder` for the most recent author/recorder.

semanticText.definition: Indicates whose goal this is - patient goal, practitioner goal, etc.
semanticText.comment: This is the individual or team responsible for establishing the goal, not necessarily who recorded it. Using Group is only allowed when the group represents a family or a household and should not represent groups of Practitioners.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `source` preserves the establishing-party concept but widens allowed targets to CareTeam and Group, while `recorder` separately captures responsibility for record content.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R4 `expressedBy` and R6 `source` share the same short text, definition, and W5 mapping `FiveWs.source`. R6 additionally introduces `recorder` with W5 mapping `FiveWs.author`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using `expressedBy` fail R6 validation because the property is gone. Code using generated models must rename `expressedBy` to `source` and add separate handling for `recorder`. R6 instances with both source and recorder, or with `source` targets of CareTeam/Group, cannot be losslessly represented in R4's single `expressedBy` element.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Confusing the person/team who established a goal with the person who recorded it can affect attribution and accountability.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify source versus recorder responsibility and allow team/family sources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep and clarify `expressedBy` as the source/establishing party, widen its targets, and add `recorder`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The semantic goal of distinguishing the party who established the goal from the party who recorded it is sound. The breaking rename from `expressedBy` to `source`, however, was not necessary to accomplish that goal: R6 could have retained the old element name, clarified that it means source, widened its targets, and added `recorder`. Living with the nonoptimal R4 name would have preserved compatibility with only moderate model-cleanliness cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking design is not to keep both `expressedBy` and `source`, but to keep `expressedBy` as the source element, update its definition/comment, allow the new CareTeam/Group-style source targets, and add `recorder` for authoring responsibility. This would preserve R4 instances and avoid same-resource duplicate source representations. The tradeoff is that R6 would retain an older, less transparent element name instead of the cleaner `source` name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves a less clear legacy element name and forgoes the cleaner `source` name, but avoids duplicate source fields and keeps R4 instances valid.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `expressedBy` as 0..1 Reference to Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or RelatedPerson.
R6 defines `source` with the same source semantics and adds CareTeam and Group targets.
R6 adds `recorder` as 0..1 Reference for the individual who recorded the Goal and takes responsibility for its content.

examples.examplesMd: A simple R4 `expressedBy` maps to R6 `source`. R6 examples with a CareTeam source or separate recorder need extensions or Provenance for R4.

findings.narrativeMd: `Goal.expressedBy` is gone in R6. The best match is `Goal.source`, but R6 also adds `Goal.recorder`, turning one old attribution field plus Provenance guidance into two core elements. This is a validation break for old instances and a model break for code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `expressedBy` is not valid in R6. R6 `source` can map back to R4 `expressedBy` only when the target is one of the old allowed target types and no distinct recorder needs to be preserved in the core Goal resource. A separate R6 `recorder` has no R4 Goal element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `expressedBy` to R6 `source`. If local R4 Provenance identified a recorder, consider populating R6 `recorder`. For R6-to-R4, use `expressedBy` only for compatible source targets and preserve recorder or incompatible source targets with Provenance or extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic split is understandable, but the rename could have been made less disruptive by retaining `expressedBy` as a deprecated alias. The tradeoff would be duplicate representations until implementers complete migration.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The Group restrictions in R6 comments are semantic guidance, not a computable target profile refinement.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Goal.expressedBy` and R6 `Goal.source` appear to carry the same source/establishing-party concept, including the same W5 source mapping, while R6 separately adds `recorder` for authoring responsibility. Removing `expressedBy` creates an avoidable wire-name and generated-model break for existing data. The target widening to CareTeam and Group could have been done on the existing element name, and adding `recorder` does not require renaming the source element.
keyEvidence: R4 Goal.expressedBy: 0..1 Reference(Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson), W5 FiveWs.source
R6 Goal.source: 0..1 Reference with the original targets plus CareTeam and Group, W5 FiveWs.source
R6 Goal.recorder: separate 0..1 Reference for the individual who recorded the Goal, W5 FiveWs.author
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; it allows evolution, but a path rename with little apparent functional necessity still deserves scrutiny.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 instances with expressedBy fail R6 validation and generated clients must rename source attribution logic; R6-to-R4 can also lose recorder or new source target detail.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep expressedBy as the establishing-party/source element, widen its targets, clarify the comment, and add recorder. That preserves R4 instances without duplicate source fields; the main tradeoff is retaining a less transparent legacy name.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Yes alternative judgment; this is a direct rename where a compatible design seems straightforward.

findings.title: Goal outcomeCode and outcomeReference were removed without a direct R6 Goal replacement

oldState.summary: R4 had repeating outcome fields for coded outcomes and Observation references.

semanticText.short: What result was achieved regarding the goal? / Observation that resulted from goal
semanticText.definition: Identifies the change (or lack of change) at the point when the status of the goal is assessed; details of what's changed (or not changed).
semanticText.comment: The goal outcome is independent of the outcome of the related activities.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 directly represented Goal outcomes as either coded results or references to Observation resources.

newState.summary: R6 Goal has no `outcomeCode` or `outcomeReference` elements.
newState.narrativeMd: No same-name or obvious direct replacement appears in the R6 Goal StructureDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 Goal differential and snapshot contain no outcome element and no same-definition replacement. `Goal.addresses` has different purpose text and represents context for why the goal exists, not the result achieved.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 Goal carrying `outcomeCode` or `outcomeReference` will be invalid against the R6 Goal schema. Because no direct R6 Goal element remains, migration is not a simple rename and may require external Observation links, extensions, notes, or profile-specific rules.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Outcome data records whether a goal was achieved, changed, or not changed; dropping it can materially affect care-plan review and quality measurement.

justification.inferredGoal: Move outcome tracking out of the Goal core resource or simplify Goal's content model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated outcome elements for a transition period or add a formal replacement relationship before removal.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The computable definitions show removal of clinically meaningful outcome fields without a direct R6 Goal replacement or supplied rationale. Simplifying Goal or moving outcomes elsewhere may be reasonable, but the level of breakage is not clearly justified without a formal replacement path. A less-breaking base design is available only partially because retaining the fields would undercut a goal of fully retiring the old representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep `outcomeCode` and `outcomeReference` as deprecated base elements for one cycle, or introduce a formal replacement relationship before removing them. That would preserve R4-valid outcome data and give implementers a staged migration path. The tradeoff is material: R6 would continue to validate a representation it may want to move out of Goal, and deprecated outcome fields could remain in production indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Protects historical outcome data but prolongs an outcome-on-Goal representation that R6 may be trying to retire or relocate.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `outcomeCode` as 0..* CodeableConcept with example binding to clinical findings.
R6 Goal contains no `outcomeCode` or `outcomeReference` element.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example uses a placeholder extension URL to illustrate that a standard or local preservation strategy is needed; it is not an HL7-defined cross-version extension.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 had two explicit outcome elements on Goal, but R6 removes both. This is the clearest data-loss risk in the Goal comparison because outcome content is clinically meaningful and no direct core R6 Goal element replaces it.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with either outcome element are R6-invalid. This is primarily an R4-to-R6 validation and migration problem; it does not arise from R6-to-R4 because R6 no longer has these fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 Goals using outcome fields before migration. Decide whether to preserve coded outcomes in extensions, convert referenced Observations into external resources with a documented relationship, place human-readable summaries in `note`, or use profile-specific rules. Test completed, not-achieved, and partially achieved goals separately.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Without rationale, the hard removal appears avoidable. A deprecation period or formal replacement mapping would have reduced breakage and protected historical outcome data while still allowing R6 to guide new implementations away from these fields.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Narrative spec pages or official change notes are needed to determine the intended R6 replacement pattern, if any.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed Goal-level outcome content through `outcomeCode` and `outcomeReference`; R6 has no direct Goal element for either. Existing R4 instances with outcome data become invalid and the migration path is not a simple rename. Outcome information can be clinically meaningful when reviewing whether a goal was achieved or what changed, so removal without a computable replacement is a real data-loss risk.
keyEvidence: R4 Goal.outcomeCode: 0..* CodeableConcept for the result achieved regarding the goal
R4 Goal.outcomeReference: 0..* Reference(Observation) for details of what changed
R6 Goal snapshot contains no outcomeCode, outcomeReference, or same-definition replacement element
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use reduces the stability burden compared with mature or normative content, but outcome data is central enough to goal review that the break remains concerning.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and R6-to-R4 loss: R4 outcome elements are unknown in R6, and migration may require Observation linkage, extensions, notes, or profile-specific decisions rather than a base element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design could retain deprecated outcomeCode/outcomeReference for one release or define a formal replacement relationship before removal. That would prolong an outcome-on-Goal representation that R6 may be trying to retire, but it would better protect existing outcome data.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the primary evidence supports a hard break with no direct R6 Goal replacement.

findings.title: Goal.lifecycleStatus required value set adds the R6-only code unknown

oldState.summary: R4 required binding to `goal-status|4.0.1` allowed proposed, planned, accepted, active, on-hold, completed, cancelled, entered-in-error, and rejected.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local CodeSystem concepts were compared directly. A terminology server expansion was not run.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 lifecycle status is mandatory, modifier, and required-bound to the R4 Goal status codes.

newState.summary: R6 required binding to `goal-status|6.0.0-ballot4` adds `unknown` and says it is for legacy data and strongly discouraged.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 local CodeSystem adds `unknown` with definition `The source system does not specify which of the values currently applies for this goal.`

semanticText.comment: It would be unusual for a recorder of a goal to not know this value; it is included to support legacy data and is strongly discouraged.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 widens the required value set by one code while retaining the same mandatory modifier element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The added code does not break R4-to-R6 validation because all R4 status codes remain available. It does break down-conversion when an R6 instance uses `lifecycleStatus=unknown`, because R4's required binding does not include that code. Since the element is a modifier, substituting another status can be clinically misleading.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Unknown lifecycle status changes the interpretation of whether a Goal should be pursued, displayed, or trusted.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow migration of legacy data where the source status is not known.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; adding `unknown` widens the R6 required value set and preserves all R4 lifecycle-status codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue because no R4 lifecycle-status code is removed. The R6 comment gives a concrete compatibility rationale: `unknown` supports legacy data and is strongly discouraged for ordinary use. The resulting R6-to-R4 representability risk is real, but the R6 widening itself is justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 preservation; R4 instances continue to validate for this element. Using an extension for `unknown` would be a down-conversion or backport strategy, not a less-breaking R6 base design, and it would make the mandatory modifier status less truthful in R6.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 down-conversion and enum updates remain concerns, but they are not less-breaking base-design alternatives for R4-to-R6 compatibility.

evidence.detail: R4 binds lifecycleStatus to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/goal-status|4.0.1` with required strength.
R6 binds lifecycleStatus to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/goal-status|6.0.0-ballot4` with required strength and includes `unknown` in the short display.
R6 CodeSystem adds `unknown`; R4 CodeSystem does not contain it.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is R6-valid for the lifecycleStatus code but fails R4 required binding validation.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `unknown` to the required lifecycle status code set. This is a forward-compatible widening for R4-to-R6, but it is a hard R6-to-R4 representability issue because R4 required bindings cannot accept that code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid status code is removed, so old instances remain valid for this field. R6 instances using `unknown` cannot validate as R4. Strict enum code generation also needs a new enum member in R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, do not silently map `unknown` to `active`, `planned`, or another concrete status. Preserve it with an extension or reject/manual-review the down-conversion. Update enum switches and UI rules to handle `unknown` explicitly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The code addition is likely justified to avoid fabricating a lifecycle status for legacy data. The backward-compatible alternative of using an extension would avoid changing the required value set but would make the core modifier element less truthful.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Adding `unknown` to the R6 required lifecycle-status value set does not make any R4 Goal invalid in R6. It is a forward-compatible widening, and the R6 comment says `unknown` is for legacy data and is strongly discouraged. A plain R4 down-conversion cannot represent that new code without an extension or local policy, but that is the ordinary cost of a new R6 code rather than a reason to revisit the R6 base design.
keyEvidence: R4 Goal.lifecycleStatus binds required to ValueSet goal-status|4.0.1
R6 Goal.lifecycleStatus binds required to ValueSet goal-status|6.0.0-ballot4 and includes short display with unknown
R6 CodeSystem goal-status adds code unknown with definition that the source system does not specify which value applies
freshReview.fmmEffect: Goal FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; because the change is widening for R4-to-R6 and the new code is discouraged, FMM does not increase concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 instance using lifecycleStatus=unknown cannot be represented by R4's required binding, but all R4 lifecycle-status values remain acceptable in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6. Avoiding the new code or moving it to an extension would preserve down-conversion but would make R6 less truthful for legacy records with genuinely unknown status.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Not applicable alternative judgment; I agree it is reverse-only, but I treat the practical compatibility concern as low enough for No problem.

findings.title: R6 adds a structured Goal.acceptance backbone with required participant when present

oldState.summary: R4 Goal has no core acceptance backbone.
oldState.narrativeMd: Stakeholder acceptance could only be represented outside the core Goal content, for example by extensions or related workflow artifacts.

newState.summary: R6 adds 0..* `Goal.acceptance` with mandatory `participant`, optional required-bound `status`, and optional `priority`.
newState.narrativeMd: Each R6 acceptance entry must identify a participant and can express agree/disagree/pending status and stakeholder-specific priority.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional element addition does not invalidate R4 instances when moving to R6. However, R6 instances can now carry structured stakeholder acceptance data that has no R4 Goal element, and strict R4 parsers will reject `acceptance`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Agreement or disagreement by patients, practitioners, teams, or organizations can affect whether a goal should be pursued.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent participant-specific acceptance and priority in the core Goal resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional R6 `acceptance` content does not invalidate R4 Goal instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of standardizing participant-specific acceptance and priority is reasonable, and the backbone is optional, so existing R4 instances are preserved. The required `participant` child only constrains R6 instances that choose to use `acceptance`; it does not make old data invalid. Therefore the base R6 addition is justified under the backward-compatibility calibration.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: An extension-only approach could help R4 systems carry similar data, but that is a backport/down-conversion mitigation rather than a backward-compatible alternative required to preserve R4-valid instances. Making the semantics core in R6 improves consistency for validators, profiles, and implementations while avoiding R4-to-R6 breakage.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Plain R4 cannot carry populated R6 acceptance data without extensions, but that is an R6-to-R4 representability issue rather than an R4-to-R6 base break.

evidence.detail: R6 requires `acceptance.participant` 1..1 when an acceptance backbone is present.

examples.examplesMd: An R4 Goal cannot carry the `acceptance` array in core JSON.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a new acceptance backbone for participant-specific agreement and priority. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it is a material down-conversion and code-generation concern because R4 has no corresponding core structure.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to this addition because the backbone is optional. R6 instances that populate it are not R4-representable without extensions, and any R6 acceptance entry missing `participant` is invalid because the child is 1..1.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, consider whether local extensions or related records should populate `acceptance`. For R6-to-R4, preserve acceptance with extensions or related artifacts and test agree, disagree, pending, multiple participants, Organization/CareTeam/Group participants, and priority-only cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding optional structure is the least disruptive way to standardize this semantics in R6. A purely extension-based approach would have been more backward-compatible but less interoperable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional structured acceptance information. Because the backbone is `0..*`, existing R4 instances remain structurally valid with respect to this new feature. The required `participant` applies only when an R6 acceptance entry is present. R4 cannot natively carry populated R6 acceptance details on down-conversion, but this is new optional R6 content rather than a break in old Goal data.
keyEvidence: R4 Goal has no core acceptance backbone
R6 Goal.acceptance is 0..* BackboneElement
R6 Goal.acceptance.participant is 1..1 only within a present acceptance backbone, with optional status and priority children
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the additive optional nature of the change dominates the maturity analysis.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: none for R4-to-R6; R6-to-R4 loss only if new acceptance content is populated and a plain R4 representation is required.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is needed to preserve R4 instances. Keeping acceptance extension-only would ease backports but would reduce the computable core support R6 is adding.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Not applicable alternative judgment; the down-conversion limitation is real, but I would not treat this optional addition as a meaningful break.

findings.title: Goal.addresses adds MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake reference targets

oldState.summary: R4 `addresses` allowed references to Condition, Observation, MedicationStatement, NutritionOrder, ServiceRequest, and RiskAssessment.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 constrained `addresses` to six resource target types.

newState.summary: R6 adds MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake to the allowed target profiles.

semanticText.definition: The identified conditions and other resources that provide the context for why the goal exists.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits additional resources to be identified as context for why the goal exists.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding reference targets is not an R4-to-R6 break. It creates a strict R4 validation break for down-converted R6 instances whose `addresses` references point to MedicationRequest, Procedure, or NutritionIntake.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping context links can make a goal less explainable and can impair workflow or care-plan review.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow goals to be connected to more types of clinical context.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; widening `addresses` target profiles preserves all R4-valid references.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake targets is a target-domain widening. No R4 target type is removed, so this finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. The broader R6 context model is clinically plausible and the compatibility cost is limited to R6-to-R4 representability and implementation updates.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed to preserve R4 instances because the old target list remains valid. Keeping the base target list narrow and relying on profiles or extensions would reduce R6-to-R4 friction, but it would also withhold standard base support for common Goal context links and is not a backward-compatible alternative in the R4-to-R6 sense.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6 references to the new target types are harder to down-convert to R4, but narrower profiles or extensions would be down-conversion mitigations, not needed R4-to-R6 alternatives.

evidence.detail: R4 target list excludes MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake.
R6 target list includes MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake.

examples.examplesMd: Each listed reference target is allowed in R6 but outside the R4 `Goal.addresses` target-profile list.

findings.narrativeMd: `Goal.addresses` is widened in R6. This is safe for R4-to-R6, but R6 data can now contain references that R4 validators and generated schemas do not allow.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No old target was removed. R6 instances using one of the three new target types are not valid R4 Goal instances without extensions or alternative relationships.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, preserve new target-type references using extensions or related resources, or reject/manual-review the conversion. Test all three new target types and mixed old/new target arrays.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The wider target list is a reasonable base-resource evolution. The backward-compatible alternative would be profile-specific allowance, but that would limit interoperability for goals related to medications, procedures, or nutrition intake.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens `Goal.addresses` by adding MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake targets while keeping the R4 target types. This preserves all R4-valid references and only creates a reverse-conversion issue for R6 instances that use the newly allowed targets. The widened list is a normal additive change to better express why a goal exists.
keyEvidence: R4 Goal.addresses targets Condition, Observation, MedicationStatement, NutritionOrder, ServiceRequest, and RiskAssessment
R6 Goal.addresses keeps those targets and adds MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake
R6 definition describes context resources for why the goal exists
freshReview.fmmEffect: Goal is FMM 2/trial-use; this does not raise concern because the change is a target-list widening, not a restriction.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: none for R4-to-R6; R6-to-R4 loss only when an R6 Goal uses a newly allowed target that R4 validators do not permit.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 design is needed. Keeping the old narrow list or requiring profiles/extensions would improve down-conversion but would withhold useful base support for common clinical context links.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Not applicable alternative judgment; I agree it is reverse-only, but the fresh path-level review classifies it as No problem.

findings.title: R6 adds Goal.continuous sustainment semantics

oldState.summary: R4 Goal has no core element indicating whether ongoing activity is needed after the goal is met.
oldState.narrativeMd: Sustainment semantics had to be inferred from descriptions, targets, care-plan context, or extensions.

semanticText.short: After meeting the goal, ongoing activity is needed to sustain the goal objective
semanticText.definition: After meeting the goal, ongoing activity is needed to sustain the goal objective.
semanticText.comment: For example, getting a yellow fever vaccination for a planned trip is a goal that is designed to be completed (continuous = false). A goal to sustain HbA1c levels would not be a one-time goal (continuous = true).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can distinguish one-time goals from goals requiring continued maintenance.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The optional addition does not invalidate R4 instances, but R6 instances that use it lose explicit sustainment semantics when converted to plain R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of sustainment semantics can affect automated achievement-status updates and reminders, but the field is optional.

justification.inferredGoal: Support automated handling of goals that must be sustained after being met.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional R6 `continuous` sustainment semantics do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 requirements text identifies a concrete programmatic need: systems can handle goals that require ongoing activity after being met. Because `continuous` is optional and additive, it does not create an R4-to-R6 validation break. The base R6 change is therefore justified despite R6-to-R4 data-loss risk.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is required for forward compatibility; old Goal instances remain valid. Keeping sustainment semantics extension-only would help R4 backports, but it would make the behavior less visible to general-purpose R6 validators and applications and is best understood as a down-conversion strategy, not an alternative needed to avoid R4-to-R6 breakage.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 cannot natively preserve the boolean on down-conversion, but extension preservation is a mitigation rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `continuous` as 0..1 boolean with sustainment semantics.

examples.examplesMd: A plain R4 Goal has no field equivalent to `continuous`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `continuous` to say whether a goal needs ongoing activity after the target is met. This is an R6-only semantic addition rather than a forward validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 instances are unaffected because the element is optional. R6-to-R4 conversion loses the boolean unless an extension or local convention is used.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, infer `continuous` only from reliable local rules. For R6-to-R4, preserve the value in an extension if automated sustainment behavior matters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A core optional boolean is a reasonable way to standardize the behavior. Keeping it extension-only would be more backward-compatible but less interoperable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `Goal.continuous` to indicate whether ongoing activity is needed after meeting the goal. This does not invalidate any R4 instance and does not change an existing R4 path. Plain R4 loses this explicit sustainment flag on down-conversion, but it is an optional new semantic field with an obvious extension or profile mitigation if backporting is important.
keyEvidence: R4 Goal has no continuous element
R6 Goal.continuous is 0..1 boolean
R6 comment gives examples such as one-time vaccination versus sustained HbA1c control
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the additive optional field does not create a stability concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: none for R4-to-R6; R6-to-R4 loss only for a new optional boolean when converting to plain R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is required. Leaving the concept extension-only would preserve R4 symmetry but reduce visibility for R6 validators and applications.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Low impact and Not applicable alternative judgment; the concern is limited to optional new R6 content.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, type, kind, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag remain the same. Status/maturity metadata changed and is recorded as a notable non-breaking change.
No same-path local Goal element had a minimum or maximum cardinality tightened. New R6 elements are optional at the parent level; removed/replaced elements are reported as findings.
Same-path choice elements `start[x]`, `target.detail[x]`, and `target.due[x]` kept their R4 type choices. Type/representation changes for replaced elements are captured in findings.

The local `gol-1` target invariant remains present with the same practical rule: target `detail` and `measure` must appear together when detail is present. Base `dom-*`, `ele-*`, and `ext-*` expression changes were excluded as inherited.
`Goal.lifecycleStatus` remains a modifier in both versions. No local same-path Goal element changed modifier status.
Common local same-path summary flags are materially stable. Summary status of added/removed fields follows from their individual findings.
No local Goal slicing changes were identified in the compared StructureDefinitions.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were identified for Goal.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit changes were identified.
No wire-format change was identified beyond normal FHIR element-name/type changes. Serialization and generated-class impacts from removed, renamed, and added fields are captured in findings.
Major R6-only local content was checked, but a formal ConceptMap would be needed to confirm official down-conversion strategies.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology pick-lists or documentation may change from broad clinical findings toward the R6 goal-description examples.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Reviewers should not treat the wording change alone as a breaking scope expansion.
